hints: Since the right angle is at $Q$, the base and height are the lengths of $PQ$ and $QR$.
Apply the area formula: $\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PQ \times QR = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 8 = 16$.
walkthrough:
Only perpendicular lengths can be multiplied as base and height.
Find the lengths of the two perpendicular sides meeting at $Q$:
$$PQ = \sqrt{(6 - 2)^2 + (3 - 3)^2} = 4$$
$$QR = \sqrt{(6 - 6)^2 + (11 - 3)^2} = 8$$

Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle:
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times PQ \times QR = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 8 = 16$$
